title: Bind each DPAPI seal to its handle as entropy, reading the old form once
body:
## Summary
DpapiSeal calls CryptProtectData with null entropy, so a sealed credential is not bound to the handle it is filed under; one sealed file copied over another still opens (src/athena/connectors/seal.py:154).

## Description
`DpapiSeal._call` (src/athena/connectors/seal.py:147-160) passes `None` for `pOptionalEntropy` on both protect and unprotect; the file name (`_path_for`, seal.py:55) is the only link between a blob and its handle (`gmail.token`, `notion.token`, `gmail.client_secret`, ...). Anyone who can write the sealed directory but cannot mint DPAPI blobs for this user (another account with write access, a restored backup) can swap `notion.token.sealed` into `gmail.token.sealed`: it unprotects cleanly and `Vault.request` (src/athena/connectors/vault.py) then sends the Notion integration secret as a bearer to the Gmail hosts. credential-vault/encryption-at-rest: "Bind the ciphertext to its record ... a ciphertext cut from one record and pasted into another fails to open"; the registry map already records this pair as a deviation. The fix the technique prescribes: seal with the handle as entropy (e.g. `b"athena-connectors:" + name`), read with it, fall back to null entropy for a legacy blob and re-seal it bound on that read (upgrade on read), count legacy unseals, and later refuse the legacy form. `seal.py` is also used by `src/athena/channels/voice/config.py:52` (select_seal), so the voice keys change with it.

Why Lane C and not built: every bound seal is a blob an older build cannot open (it unprotects with null entropy, fails, and reads the credential as missing: "no sealed credential; reconnect it"), and upgrade-on-read rewrites existing blobs in that form. It is a stored-format change with no rollback path for a downgraded build - `irreversible` under the routing rules, as the round brief anticipated. The person's cost on a downgrade is a reconnect per connector (and re-entering any voice key), not data loss, which is the call the operator owns.

## Flow
- copy %ATHENA_HOME%/connectors/sealed/notion.token.sealed over gmail.token.sealed
- the next Gmail call: DpapiSeal.unseal('gmail.token') returns the Notion secret (null entropy on both)
- Vault.request attaches it as a bearer to gmail.googleapis.com - a credential sent to the wrong provider
- fix order: entropy on seal; unseal tries bound, then legacy, re-seals a legacy hit bound; a counter of legacy unseals on the vault view; a later commit refuses legacy

## Expected impact
A transplanted or swapped sealed file stops opening on Windows; no surface change while the upgrade is silent. What could break: an older build (or a voice config read by an older build) no longer opens credentials sealed or re-sealed by the new one.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a sealed credential opens only under the handle it was sealed for
Before: 1 of 1 transplanted blob opens (null entropy on both calls, seal.py:154; walked, Windows)
After: 0 of 1 would open under the wrong handle; a legacy blob opens once and is re-sealed bound (predicted)
Method: simulation - three walked cases (transplant, legacy read, fresh seal); a Windows-only pytest (skipif not win32) is the instrument, not built because the change is gated
Result: better
Gate: irreversible
evidence:
src/athena/connectors/seal.py:153-154
        # The entropy and the prompt struct are both null: the user's logon is the key.
        ok = fn(ctypes.byref(blob_in), None, None, None, None, 0, ctypes.byref(blob_out))
src/athena/connectors/seal.py:55-57 _path_for: the handle is only the file name
src/athena/channels/voice/config.py:52 imports select_seal (a second consumer of the format)
.ai/registry-map.json connector-service x credential-vault: state deviation, evidence names seal.py:150

title: Connector acts that widen what Athena may send leave no record
body:
## Summary
Turning a connector's writes on, widening its allow-list, connecting and disconnecting are recorded nowhere but the current state of connections.json (src/athena/daemon/connectors.py:56-82, src/athena/connectors/vault.py set_writes/set_allowlist).

## Description
`connector_act` (src/athena/daemon/connectors.py) applies `set_writes`, `set_allowlist`, `connect_token`, `disconnect` and `probe` and answers the new view; `Vault._changed` saves the record and re-merges the catalog. Nothing appends an episode, a ledger row or a log line for the act: after the fact there is no way to say when writes were turned on for Gmail, which recipients were added and when, or that a connect replaced one account with another (ADR 0062's reset is a `notice` that the next connect overwrites). AGENTS.md "Ledger everything" covers model invocations; the connector acts that change what a model may send outside the machine are the gap. credential-vault golden path (custody: "telling the truth about its state") and governance-and-records/audit-logging (an append-only record of security-relevant changes). What fixed looks like: one append-only row per act - connector, act, the switch values before and after, the account key, the time - never a value.

## Flow
- POST /connectors/gmail/settings {"writes_enabled": true, "allowlist": ["x@y"]}
- connections.json now says writes on and the list; the previous values are gone
- no episode, ledger row or log line says the change happened
- a later question 'since when could Athena mail x@y?' has no answer

## Expected impact
The operator (or a reviewer of an incident) can reconstruct when sending was widened. What could break: nothing at runtime; the open question is where the row lives (the brain's episodes, the ledger, or a vault-side journal) and what it may name.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every write-widening connector act leaves one record
Before: 0 records for 5 act kinds (grep: no ledger/episode/logger call in daemon/connectors.py or the vault's switch setters)
After: 5 of 5 acts recorded (predicted)
Method: simulation - the acts walked through the route and the vault; the instrument is a route test reading the chosen store, unbuildable until the store is chosen
Result: better
Gate: architecture
evidence:
grep -n "logger\.|ledger|append" src/athena/daemon/connectors.py src/athena/connectors/vault.py
  vault.py:88 logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
  vault.py:370 logger.warning("%s", self.records_notice)   # the only log call: an unreadable records file
src/athena/connectors/vault.py set_writes / set_allowlist / disconnect -> _changed -> _save (state only)

title: Every connector list render unseals the OAuth client id just to say yes or no
body:
## Summary
`Vault.view` calls `client_kept`, which unseals the sealed client id (DPAPI decrypt, or a keychain read that can prompt) on every `GET /connectors` render, only to answer a boolean (src/athena/connectors/vault.py client_kept, view).

## Description
`client_kept` (src/athena/connectors/vault.py, ADR 0117) returns `bool(self._get(connector_id, "client_id"))`: a full unseal of a stored value, per OAuth connector, per list render and per act reply (every `connector_act` answers `vault.view`). credential-vault/encryption-at-rest, memory hygiene: "Plaintext exists between unseal and use. Its lifetime is minimized" - this unseal has no use; and on a keyring seal each read is a keychain access a locked macOS keychain answers with a prompt. Fixed: the vault records `client_kept` on the ConnectionRecord when it seals or drops the pair (`_admit`, `_drop`), reads that for the view, and a record from before the field is filled once on load (one unseal, then never again).

## Flow
- the desktop polls GET /connectors
- Vault.views -> view('gmail') -> client_kept -> _get -> seal.unseal('gmail.client_id')
- plaintext client id created and dropped, per render
- fix: a record flag written at seal/drop time; a one-time backfill for old records

## Expected impact
No plaintext created by a list render; no keychain prompt from a poll. What could break: a record flag that drifts from the seal (a seal wiped out of band) says kept when it is not - the reconnect then answers the existing 'no client is kept' refusal.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - zero unseals per list render
Before: 1 unseal per OAuth connector per GET /connectors and per act reply (read: view -> client_kept -> _get)
After: 0 per render, 1 per record ever (predicted)
Method: simulation - call path read; the counting-seal test is the instrument, not built because the record shape change and its backfill are M with a desktop consumer of the view
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/athena/connectors/vault.py view(): "client_kept": self.client_kept(connector_id)
src/athena/connectors/vault.py client_kept(): return bool(self._get(connector_id, "client_id"))
src/athena/daemon/connectors.py connector_act: every act answers vault.view(connector_id)
instrument: a route test with a counting seal: GET /connectors N times, count unseal calls (Before: 1 per OAuth connector per render); plus a load test of an old-format record that lacks the new flag

title: A settled consent flow stays in every connector view for the daemon's life
body:
## Summary
FlowManager keeps every flow it started; `Vault.view` reports the connector's last flow forever, so after a disconnect the view still carries `flow: {phase: done, detail: "connected as ..."}` (src/athena/connectors/oauth.py FlowManager, src/athena/connectors/vault.py view).

## Description
`FlowManager.add` (src/athena/connectors/oauth.py) only removes a flow when a newer one for the same connector replaces it; `cancel_all` clears on stop. Nothing removes a flow that settled. `Vault.view` adds `"flow": flow.view()` for the connector, and `disconnect` does not touch flows. So a disconnected Gmail is listed with a done flow saying it is connected as the old account, and a failed one ('the consent page was not answered in time') keeps saying so until the next connect. Whether the desktop renders that line is the open half: the panel reads `flow` while it polls after connect (daemon/connectors.py docstring). Fixed: a disconnect, and a later successful token or OAuth admission, forget the connector's settled flow; the view's `flow` is null unless one is in progress or just settled.

## Flow
- connect Gmail through OAuth; the flow settles done
- disconnect Gmail
- GET /connectors: connection.status disconnected, flow.phase done, flow.detail 'connected as me@...'

## Expected impact
A disconnected or reconnected connector no longer carries a stale consent outcome. What could break: a surface that polls `flow` right after a done connect must read it before the next act clears it.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the view's flow describes the current connection attempt only
Before: 1 stale flow per OAuth connector after disconnect (walked: FlowManager has no removal on settle)
After: 0 (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked through FlowManager and view; the route test is S, but whether the desktop shows the stale line needs the rendered panel
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/athena/connectors/oauth.py FlowManager.add: removes only other flows of the same connector; no removal on done/failed
src/athena/connectors/vault.py view(): flow = self.flows.for_connector(connector_id) ... "flow": flow.view()
src/athena/connectors/vault.py disconnect(): no self.flows call
instrument: a route test: OAuth flow to done, then disconnect, then GET /connectors - assert the view's flow is null or names the disconnect (Before: phase done, 'connected as ...'); plus the desktop Accounts render of that view
